item.description: CHICAGO, IL - OCTOBER 22: Zavier Scott #30 of the Chicago Bears runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears have a 16-man practice squad, but the list will be fluid, and we’ll update it throughout the year. UPDATE (10/27): The Bears signed running back Zavier Scott to the 53-man roster. Caden Barnett, OG Christian Jones, OT Salvon Ahmed, RB Kaden Davis, WR J.P. Richardson, WR Scotty Miller, WR Stephen Carlson, TE Qadir Ismail, TE Miller Moss, QB Wayne Matthews III, LB Buddy Johnson, LB Keidron Smith, S Elijah Jones, CB KC Eziomume, CB Beau Gardner, LS Practice squad injured: Anthony Johnson Jr. (S) Here are the qualifications for practice squad eligibility and some rules to remember. A 17th player is permitted as long as he qualifies for the NFL’s International Pathway Program. Players with no accrued seasons (rookies) and those with fewer than nine regular-season games in their lone accrued season. A maximum of ten players are allowed who have earned no more than two accrued seasons. Up to six players with unlimited accrued seasons are permitted on the practice squad. However, the number of players in the last two categories cannot exceed 10 total players. Teams can elevate up to two practice squad players for each game, but they can still only have 48 players active on game day. After the game, the elevated player(s) will revert to the practice squad. A player can be elevated up to three times, but if he’s needed after that, the team would be required to sign him to the 53-man active roster. Players on practice squads are free agents who can be signed to another team’s active roster. A player’s current club can’t block him from leaving; they can only make a counteroffer to keep him. Ultimately, it’s the player’s decision. If a player is signed away, his new team must keep him on its 53-man roster for three weeks, but if he’s released, he’ll revert to his previous team. Players signed to another active roster are also guaranteed three weeks’ salary. A practice squad player can’t sign with his team’s upcoming opponent unless he does so six days before the upcoming game or ten days prior if his team is on its bye week.

item.title: Lancs treatment of Anderson 'disrespectful' - Broad
item.description: Stuart Broad (left) and James Anderson (right) led England's bowling attack together for a generation until the former retired at the end of the 2023 Ashes [Getty Images] Lancashire have been "pretty disrespectful" in their treatment of legendary bowler James Anderson, says his long-time England bowler partner Stuart Broad. Anderson, 44, was told last week he will not have his contract renewed by the Red Rose county, ending his 26-year professional career with the club. Anderson took 50 wickets in the County Championship last season and served as captain, but incoming director of cricket Paul Farbrace has decided he wants to rebuild the struggling side, who finished second bottom in Division Two of the County Championship, for the future without England's all-time leading wicket-taker. "I didn't like it from Lancashire," Broad said on the For Love of Cricket podcast. "It was not done in the right way. I think it was disrespectful. "You give your icons or greats of the game a better send off than that." Is this the end for Jimmy Anderson? Lancashire consider Anderson farewell amid fan unrest Farbrace, who moved from Sussex at the end of the season, has not yet officially started in his new role at Lancashire but delivered the news to Anderson at a meeting last week alongside chief executive Richard Kenyon, who has also recently been appointed. The news was first reported on Wednesday and Lancashire did not comment officially until Sunday. At a meeting with members on Monday, the club said they would look into arranging Anderson a farewell . "It shows a lack of leadership at that club," said Broad, whose combined total of Test wickets with Anderson stands at a record 1,039 in 138 Tests. "It shows a lack of doing it the right way. "Paul Farbrace is new, but where is the chair? Where is the board demanding that this is done in a better way?" Speaking publicly for the first time since the decision on Sunday, Anderson, who also had his England career cut short in 2024 in similar circumstances , expressed his sadness at the situation but stopped short of retiring. Other counties are understood to be interested in signing the veteran. "I get the thought process, 'we could probably get two half-decent cricketers for the one and losing that salary'," Broad added. "It doesn't surprise me that some counties have already been on the phone and seeing what his interest levels are. "I don't know what his next steps are. I think his statement was quite interesting. "There will be a lot of counties that want him. He offers a huge amount, he's still one of the best bowlers in the country." item.title: Ravens discussion: should Eric DeCosta have traded for Quenton Nelson?
item.description: Quenton Nelson Indianapolis Colts offensive guard Quenton Nelson (56) walks off the field following their game at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sept. 9, 2018. The Indianapolis Colts lost to the Cincinnati Bengals 34-23.Indianapolis Colts Play The Cincinnati Bengals In Their 2018 Season Opener | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Ravens made a blockbuster trade for offensive line a few weeks ago, but they may have been outdone by the Seahawks on Tuesday. Eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson is heading from Indianapolis to Seattle in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, per The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero . Baltimore’s offensive line issues have been glaring (again) this year, and rookie guard Vega Ioane is now set to miss time with a sprained MCL. Nelson would certainly upgrade the unit, potentially at right guard initially before taking over for John Simpson at left guard after Ioane’s return. But after sending a 2028 second-rounder to the Eagles for Cam Jurgens a few weeks ago, does trading even more draft capital make sense considering the Ravens’ current and future salary cap picture? Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s thoughts Nikhil Mehta I have always loved Quenton Nelson, so in my heart of hearts, I would have loved to make this trade. But, partially because I am expecting my colleagues to be all for it, I’ll play devil’s advocate. Seattle’s 2027 third and 2028 fifth are valued somewhere in the second-round range – higher or lower depending on how you value the Day 3 pick. But the Seahawks can absorb all of the roughly $10 million Nelson is owed over the remainder of the season. The Ravens cannot, which would force them to restructure current contracts and/or ask the Colts to eat some of Nelson’s salary. The former exacerbates an already-untenable 2027 cap situation; the latter would drive the trade price up, likely requiring a second-round pick and potentially a Day 3 kicker to complete the deal. Nelson is also on an expiring deal, and like it or not, Baltimore has $5.5 million in guaranteed money committed to John Simpson next year. Nelson is definitely an upgrade this year, but can Baltimore get a long-term deal done? If not, second-round value is a high price for a half-season rental, especially considering the sobering reality that the 2026 Ravens may not be a Super Bowl-caliber team. They may need another year to remake their roster under Jesse Minter’s new coaching staff to reach their full potential. The upshot of a rental, though, is worth mentioning. Nelson decidedly pushes Baltimore closer to championship contention, and if he walks in free agency, the Ravens should be in line for at least a fourth-, if not a third-round compensatory pick in 2028. item.title: Lens fans banned from Anfield for Champions League clash with Liverpool after flares chaos
item.description: Lens supporters have been banned from attending a Champions League fixture against Liverpool at Anfield after Uefa's appeals judges barred the French club from selling them tickets for away games in the competition. The ban will be served when Lens travel to Leipzig on 24 November and to Liverpool at Anfield on 27 January, with a third game ban deferred for a two-year probationary period. The ruling on Tuesday came after Lens fans lit dozens of flares and threw some toward rival supporters and the field during the team's Champions League game at Club Brugge last week, forcing the match to be stopped briefly. Lens went on to lose the match 3-0, and they are currently 27th in the league phase table after taking three points from three matches so far. Lens fans have been banned from attending two Champions League away matches (AP) The club was already on probation by Uefa for fans lighting flares and fireworks at a previous Champions League game at Slavia Prague in September. Uefa said Lens have been fined 80,000 euros (£67,000) for charges of “lighting and throwing of pyrotechnics as well as for acts of damage.” The ticket ban covers two Champions League away games, Uefa confirmed. The ruling means Liverpool will play January’s match with only their own fans inside the stadium as they aim to qualify for the Champions League knockout stages. Andoni Iraola’s men have taken maximum points from their opening three fixtures and are third in the Champions League standings behind PSG and Aston Villa. The Reds have also found form in the Premier League, having only lost one of their first eight matches in England’s top-flight this season. A 2-0 win over Brighton on Sunday lifted Liverpool into fourth place, just a point behind the Seagulls and six adrift of Manchester City and Arsenal. Liverpool are due to return to Champions League action next week when they face Turkish side Fenerbahce away from home. This follows a Carabao Cup clash with Chelsea on Wednesday before a mouthwatering league match against Arsenal at Anfield on Sunday. Their final game before the November international break will be a trip to Crystal Palace on 8 November.

item.title: Ajay Mitchell infuses OKC Thunder with excitement and hope after injuries | Carlson
item.description: Ajay Mitchell dribbled left around a couple of Phoenix defenders, sensed an opening and zipped to the basket, finger-rolling the ball through the hoop. Less than a minute later, he caught the ball, got a step on his defender and drove hard, this time drawing contact and a shooting foul. Then on the very next Suns possession, he picked up Devin Booker , and when the Phoenix star went low with the ball, Mitchell got a hand on it and batted it out of bounds. All of that before the first TV timeout. More: OKC Thunder fans show love for injured stars Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace on somber night It was a reminder of the past. Oh, yeah, remember this version of Ajay Mitchell? He cooked in the playoffs last season. But it was also a reminder for the future. All is not lost without Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. As the Thunder returned to the court less than a day after losing not one but two starters to long-term injuries — both await surgery, Williams for a fractured fibula and dislocated ankle , Wallace for a torn labrum in his shoulder — the franchise faced a night unlike any other in its history. The Thunder needed a chance to regroup and recover. It needed an off day. It got a game against the Suns instead. And darned if the Thunder didn’t win 125-114 . What’s more, OKC led all but 17 seconds of the game. That was because every Thunder who played had a hand in the victory, guys like rookie Bennett Stirtz, who played 24 minutes, and two-way player Josh Dix, who played 22. Contributions from everyone have to be the norm for as long as Williams and Wallace are sidelined. But no player’s contribution ticked up more than Mitchell’s. He scored a career-high 30 points on 10-of-16 shooting, adding five assists, two rebounds and one block. Mitchell was plus-18, the best of any Thunder. “We saw it last year,” Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said of Mitchell’s ability to have a big impact on a game. “If you zoom out to his whole trajectory as a player, he was pretty functional and impactful even as a rookie player on a very good team, before he took an injury that year, and then obviously had almost a linear trajectory last year with the way that he started and finished the season. “I think he’s kind of established that he’s a great player and that he’s got a really bright future.” True, but stepping into this new reality for the first time, Mitchell looks like he’s got a really bright present. He can score and create offensively, and he can hold his own against a lot of players defensively. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander believes that versatility has actually made things difficult for Mitchell. “He kind of gets swung around in terms of his role just because guys are in and out of the lineup,” SGA said. “But it seems like whatever we need from him, he provides at a high level, and I expect the same thing from Ajay going forward. “Guys are out, and we need more scoring? item.title: Marcos Rojo case: document that could put Fla in the Libertadores final
item.description: Marcos Rojo case: document that could put Fla in the Libertadores final The Libertadores semifinals concluded on the pitch last week, but the battle for a place in the final continues. Flamengo are still hoping to overturn their elimination by Estudiantes through the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS). The result on the pitch could be overturned because Marcos Rojo's inclusion in the lineup may be ruled ineligible. No date has yet been set for a final decision. Several journalists published the body's interim ruling on the case this Tuesday (27), and OneFootball helps you understand the situation in three points: 1. Clearance to play The ruling signed by Antonio de Quesada of CAS allowed Rojo to play in the semifinal against Flamengo. The clearance is confirmed in two passages of the document: "The player's interest in preserving a particularly significant sporting opportunity that he may never have again outweighs, for the purposes of interim relief, the interests put forward to prevent his participation." "...the deputy president does not consider that provisionally allowing the player to participate in the match would compromise the integrity of the competition." 2. No guarantee against potential sanctions Although it allowed Rojo to take the field, the interim measure did not guarantee that Estudiantes were exempt from possible sanctions. In the document, CAS chose not to preempt a final decision on the case. Here are the passages that indicate this: "...the following request is denied: 'Order that the player's participation in accordance with this order may not be invoked by Conmebol as grounds for sporting or disciplinary sanctions against the club or the player.'" "It is not appropriate, within the scope of this request for interim relief, to issue an advance ruling on a purely hypothetical situation." 3. Estudiantes still at risk Despite granting clearance to Estudiantes, CAS warned the Argentine club about the risks of fielding Rojo. The body has yet to make a final decision on the player's eligibility, and no date has been set for it. "However, it is for Estudiantes and the player to assess the risks in the event that the final CAS award does not confirm the player's eligibility." According to ge, both Flamengo and Estudiantes are confident they can secure a favorable ruling in the case. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: 76ers make roster request due to injury that forced LeBron James into center role
item.description: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images 76ers make roster request due to injury that forced LeBron James into center role appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LeBron James can literally do it all on the basketball court, and that was evidenced by the fact that he ended up being the Philadelphia 76ers ’ starting center against the Detroit Pistons in the absence of Joel Embiid, who was rested. Embiid, just like the 76ers, has started the season strongly but Philadelphia are dealing with an obvious problem, especially after Ariel Hukporti tore his right Achilles tendon in the preseason opener against the New York Knicks. Now, the 76ers have applied for a disabled player exception due to the injury, per a post on X by Insider Jake Fischer. “Amid the NBA’s string of early-season injuries, the Philadelphia 76ers have applied for a disabled player exception, per source, in respect of Ariel Hukporti’s torn Achilles,” he wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Hukporti signed a one-year, $3.4 million contract with Philadelphia in July after winning an NBA championship with New York. He averaged 2.1 points and 2.7 rebounds in 9.1 minutes per game across 79 appearances, including six starts, over his two seasons with the Knicks. The Sixers are eligible for a disabled player exception worth approximately $1.7 million, half of Hukporti’s 2026-27 salary. However, receiving the exception would not automatically solve the problem. Philadelphia is operating under a hard cap at the first apron and sits approximately $1.8 million below that threshold, meaning they cannot sign a replacement center to a standard contract without first creating additional financial flexibility. That means that before a new center can be brought in, the 76ers will need to either waive a player or execute a trade to free up room. Philadelphia entered the season with multiple backup center options, including the likes of Adam Bona, Tacko Fall and Dominick Barlow, in addition to Hukporti. However, Bona is currently listed as day-to-day due to a left foot sprain, with Barlow and Fall out due to a lumbar spine bone stress problem and a quadriceps injury, respectively. Hence, as things stand, Embiid is their only recognized center, and it remains to be seen whether the disabled player exception ends up giving them the room for another player, if approved. item.title: How Brewers made 3 kinds of MLB history with an eight-run fifth-inning in World Series
item.description: How Brewers made 3 kinds of MLB history with an eight-run fifth-inning in World Series originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 3 of the World Series, 10-1, and it was thanks to a now record-breaking fifth inning for the Brewers. With old friend Freddy Peralta on the mound, the Brewers started off the inning with a lineout, a single, and a flyout. With a runner on first and two outs, this inning seemed close to over. But the Brewers put up eight runs in the inning. That wild inning made a lot of MLB history, with Jayson Stark of The Athletic highlighting three kinds of history that the Brewers made in this inning, all with two outs, that might never be done again. How Brewers made three kinds of MLB history with wild eight-run inning "Seven straight two-out hits in a World Series game? As those hits kept coming, one after another, I couldn't wait to fire off this question to my friends at STATS Perform: Had any team ever done that before? Nope!" Stark shared. After Christian Yelich walked, William Contreras hit an infield single, loading the bases with two outs. The Rays changed pitchers to Cameron Booser, who allowed a single to Brice Turang, a single to Garrett Mitchell, a double to Cooper Pratt, and a double to Sal Frelick before being pulled for Cole Sulser. But the hit parade didn't end, with David Hamilton hitting a single and Jackson Chourio hitting a double, before Jake Bauers flew out to mercifully end this inning. Those seven straight hits with two outs are not just a World Series record; they're also a record for any round of the postseason, making the feat that much more impressive. item.title: Australia fight back to keep Cummins out of unwanted club... for now
item.description: Australia lost the second Test in Gqeberha by an innings and 31 runs [Getty Images] Third Test, Cape Town (day one of five) South Africa 329: Ackerman 95, Markram 78; Starc 6-72 Australia: Yet to bat Scorecard It is the club every cricket captain desperately tries to avoid. Nasser Hussain is a fully paid-up member. Ricky Ponting won it all in charge of Australia, yet people still talk about his decision to bowl at Edgbaston when Glenn McGrath was on his way to hospital in 2005. The 27th October, the 2026 Cape Town decider, could yet be an occasion for which Pat Cummins is always remembered – a Test which means he joins that unfortunate group of skippers who chose to bowl when they should have opted to bat. It is down to his bowlers that that is not already all but a certainty. After a shocking start, a bad call at the toss compounded by a wayward bowling performance across the first two hours, Australia roared back into the Test in the afternoon. They were helped by some careless South African batting as their happy hookers allowed a position of 203-1 to become 232-6. Aiden Markram, David Bedingham and Wiaan Mulder were all out attempting to take on the short balls – for 78, 50 and nought respectively. On 95, opener Marques Ackerman ran past one from Nathan Lyon with the glory of a first Protea century in his second Test in his sights and captain Temba Bavuma was undone by a straight ball from Lyon. Either side of a knock of 179 last week, Bavuma has got out to off-spin three times in three innings – all for single-figure scores. And while Australia stuck to their task in the afternoon, fielding well and drying up the scoring after 140 runs were leaked at more than four runs per over in the first session, most impressive was the way Mitchell Starc thundered in the day's final moments. At 327-6, South Africa could yet have finished this enthralling day - one fitting of a series decider from which the winner will finish the series on top of the rankings – in the ascendancy. Instead, Starc took four wickets in six deliveries with the new ball, first prising out Ryan Rickelton for 42 and Marco Jansen 52. He targeted pads and stumps, bowled Gerald Coetzee and pinned Kagiso Rabada lbw for ducks. South Africa were 329 all out. Somehow, after everything, if either side is happy, it is Australia. Such is the time difference, many back home missed this fightback, having rolled over when Scott Boland was left out again, Cummins chose to bowl under blue skies and South Africa plundered the bowling through the opening session. When Starc was being slapped and steered for four consecutive fours by Ackerman, few anticipated this finale. Not since Ponting's insertion of England 21 years ago had a 100-run opening partnership been made for a side put into bat by Australia. But Cummins' Australia held firm again where other sides have folded. As a side they remain imperfect. They could yet lose this Test - a result that could have wider repercussions going forward

item.description: Clásico controversy: CTA rules Cancelo should have been booked The Technical Committee of Referees (CTA) analyzed the most contentious incidents from the recent Clásico between FC Barcelona and Real Madrid on its regular show, Tiempo de Revisión. In its weekly installment, the refereeing body issued its official verdict on the two most controversial moments from last Sunday’s match, assessing the decisions made by referee Martínez Munuera on the pitch. The first incident under scrutiny was the appeal for handball against Alejandro Balde inside the penalty area as he faced Kylian Mbappé. The committee upheld the referee’s on-field interpretation, stating that his arm was in a natural position. By contrast, the CTA did identify a disciplinary error in João Cancelo’s hard tackle on Diomande during an opposition attacking transition. According to the official explanation, the full-back caught part of the attacker’s leg as he advanced with the ball. Although the committee ruled out excessive force or brutality warranting a straight red card, it concluded that the challenge was clearly reckless and that a yellow card should have been shown. With these findings, the committee backed the referee’s judgment inside the penalty area in correctly declining to award a penalty, but highlighted the lack of disciplinary firmness in the clash between Cancelo and Diomande, formally concluding its refereeing review of a Clásico that once again reignited debate in the football world. item.title: Barcelona captain Raphinha likes video questioning Ballon d’Or criteria after Harry Kane triumph
item.description: Barcelona captain Raphinha likes video questioning Ballon d’Or criteria after Harry Kane triumph Barcelona enjoyed one of their most successful campaigns in recent years during the 2025/25 season. They secured the domestic treble under Hansi Flick. Raphinha played a leading role for Barça that season, but despite his outstanding performances, he finished only fifth in the Ballon d’Or voting the following year. According to SPORT , Raphinha has now liked a TikTok video posted by content creator Dani Quintana questioning the consistency of the award’s criteria following Harry Kane’s victory on Monday. Raphinha’s 2024/25 campaign compared with Kane’s success Kane secured the 2026 Ballon d’Or after an extraordinary campaign with Bayern Munich, recording 73 goals and eight assists in 65 appearances. The Englishman also won three domestic trophies and reached the Champions League semi-finals. Quintana highlighted the similarities between the Englishman’s accolades and Raphinha’s achievements a year earlier. Raphinha finished 5th in the Ballon d’Or rankings last year. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The Brazilian helped Barcelona win La Liga , the Copa del Rey and the Spanish Super Cup while reaching the Champions League semi-finals. He recorded 56 goal contributions and finished as both the leading scorer and assist provider in Europe’s elite competition. Despite those achievements, Raphinha finished fifth in the 2025 Ballon d’Or rankings, with Ousmane Dembele eventually claiming the award following PSG’s triumph. One of the biggest Ballon d’Or snubs in recent times The 2025 Ballon d’Or continues to be one of the most debated in recent times due to Raphinha’s final position in the voting. While no one can argue that Ousmane Dembele didn’t deserve it, Raphinha finishing fifth felt too low for the kind of season he had. Harry Kane was awarded the Ballon d’Or last night. (Photo by Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images) Kane’s 73-goal campaign certainly deserves recognition, and his scoring numbers were considerably higher. However, Raphinha’s influence extended beyond just finishing chances, as he helped Barça with his creativity, pressing and attacking movement. The Englishman, after a very similar season in terms of overall accolades, now finds himself a Ballon d’Or winner. Ultimately, different seasons produce different candidates, making direct comparisons imperfect. Nevertheless, Raphinha was treated unfairly last season and will hope to put in an excellent campaign this time around to give himself a chance next year.

The world number three let slip three match points in the second set before overturning a 3-1 deficit in the tie-break. He sealed progression in two hours and four minutes with a deft volley at the net, and will next face Austrian wild card Jurij Rodionov or last week's Almaty finalist Nikoloz Basilashvili. Alcaraz, making his first appearance at the ATP 500 event since 2021, extended his unbeaten run at that level to 22 matches. He is chasing his fourth tour-level title of the season after triumphs at the Australian Open, Doha and Tokyo. The seven-time Grand Slam champion missed much of the 2026 season, including the French Open and Wimbledon, with a wrist injury before returning to action at the US Open. In women's tennis, Venus Williams suffered a straight-sets defeat to a player almost 28 years her junior as her return to competition ended in a first-round exit at the Guangzhou Open. The 46-year-old American was beaten 6-2, 6-2 by 18-year-old Austrian Lilli Tagger, extending her losing run in singles to 16 matches dating back to July 2025. Seven-time Grand Slam champion Williams last competed at the US Open, where she lost to Sofia Kenin in the first round and also suffered defeat in her opening doubles match alongside her sister Serena. Fourth seed Tagger - the 2025 French Open girls' singles champion - has enjoyed a breakthrough season, winning her maiden WTA Tour title in Prague earlier this year. The world number 53, who is regarded by some as a future grand slam contender, hit 29 winners to set up a last-16 meeting with Poland's Magda Linette.

item.description: Napoli coach Massimiliano Allegri is not appealing against his two-match ban after his red card against Roma (ANDREA PATTARO) Napoli coach Massimiliano Allegri was on Tuesday banned for two Serie A matches and fined following his red card late in his team's 3-3 draw against Roma last weekend. He will miss the Wednesday's match at Monza and Sunday's trip to Juventus. While the club posted a statement on its website saying it would appeal, their coach said he would not. "I've decided not to appeal because you never know - instead of a two-match suspension, I could end up with four," he said. "What upsets me the most - more than being suspended - is that we didn't come away with the three points despite our strong performance," he added. "But in any case, whoever is on the bench will surely do a better job than I would," added Allegri, who has been criticised since his arrival in Naples the summer. item.title: 2026 Mexico Open odds: Why favorite Wyndham Clark the best bet to win
item.description: The PGA Tour makes a quick turn from Port Royal in Bermuda to Vidanta Vallarta this week, where the Mexico Open will be contested for a $6 million purse and crucial FedExCup points for fall players looking to secure 2027 playing status. Brian Campbell is the defending champion but you'll have to scroll quite a ways down to find his odds to win outright (+22500). The pretournament favorite is Wyndham Clark, a three-time winner on Tour this season including his second U.S. Open crown in June at Shinnecock. Here's a look at where Clark and the rest of the field stand ahead of the Tour's fifth fall event and first of two stops in Mexico. VidantaWorld Mexico Open odds (as of Tuesday, Oct. 27, courtesy of DraftKings) Wyndham Clark (+1300) Ben James (+1850) Doug Ghim (+1850) Tom Kim (+1900) Ben Griffin (+2050) Corey Conners (+2500) Johnny Keefer (+2700) Harry Hall (+2800) Marco Penge (+3000) Max Homa (+3100) Doug Ghim (+3100) Blades Brown (+3300) Jackson Suber (+3500) Neal Shipley (+3700) Zach Bauchou (+3700) Who will win the 2026 Mexico Open? When handicapping a tournament it's hard to tell where the line between bias against landing on the favorite outright ends and the desire to chase perceived value begins. The Mexico Open is perhaps the best juxtaposition of these two equally limited preconceptions in the 2026 Tour schedule. And this wasn't a situation anyone could have planned for but here we are: The weather in Bermuda over the weekend has created a certain level of randomness because of travel (see: chaos) that theoretically is ideal for a longshot to sneak in and topple what seems to be a top-heavy field . Add in the desperation that comes with the fall golf season, and the conditions are right for something shocking to happen south of the border. VidantaWorld Mexico Open - Rd 1 The opening round of the VidantaWorld Mexico Open is underway at Vidanta Vallarta Golf Course in Vallarta, Mexico. But ... digging into the numbers suggests that oddsmakers might actually be doing a disservice to Clark at +1300. We make him more of a 7-to-1 favorite based on his elite approach game compared to the field. item.description: The Indianapolis Colts got ahead of the trade deadline. After entering the season with playoff aspirations, Indianapolis has backslid. The Colts look more like the team that finished 2025 on a seven-game losing streak than the one that started that campaign 7-1. At 2-5, Indianapolis has already fired general manager Chris Ballard -- the man who opted to get the band back together even after last year's frustrating falloff. Now they've shipped out one of the team's most impactful starters in the face of another lost year. The Colts traded Quenton Nelson, six-time All-Pro and 2018 Ballard draftee, to the Seattle Seahawks in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. He's likely the first domino to fall as the NFL trade deadline approaches. November 10 at 4 p.m. E.T. will mark the end of deal season, at least until Super Bowl 61 is in the books. Indianapolis has set up a billboard to tell the league it's a seller. That could mean saying goodbye to one of the franchise's stars. So what lies ahead for three-time Pro Bowl tailback Jonathan Taylor? Why the Colts could trade Taylor Taylor has salary cap hits of $21 million in 2027 and $22 million in 2028, but has no remaining guaranteed money remaining on his two-year, $44 million contract extension after this season. While that wouldn't be difficult to restructure to more manageable numbers, it would also leave him as an island in a sea of rebuilding unpredictability. Daniel Jones has regressed back to the player the New York Giants couldn't fix. The receiving corps has badly underwhelmed without Alec Pierce (injury) or Michael Pittman Jr. (traded to the Steelers) in it. Taylor ran for nearly 1,600 yards and 18 touchdowns last season and still didn't make the playoffs. This year he's on pace for 1,400 rush yards and 19 touchdowns and the Colts are 2-5. There are a lot of miles on the 27-year-old's odometer. He's had more than 1,900 NFL touches on top of nearly 1,000 more in three seasons as a Wisconsin Badger. item.description: Tadhg Furlong was in Ireland training on Tuesday after he was cited for an alleged groin grab [Getty Images] Ireland's assistant coach Jonathan Sexton has backed prop Tadhg Furlong after the Leinster prop was cited for an alleged groin grab. The incident happened late in the first half of Leinster's United Rugby Championship win on Saturday when Munster back row Gavin Coombes alleged to referee Andrew Brace he had been grabbed in the groin by an unnamed Leinster player. Television match official [TMO] Colin Stanley could not find any evidence at the time, but Furlong, 33, was cited on Monday over the incident and could miss Ireland's Nations Championship fixtures if found guilty. Furlong trained with Ireland on Tuesday and, speaking after that session, Sexton said he backed his former provincial and international team-mate. "In terms of the incident, I can't say too much about it obviously, because the disciplinary process is ongoing," said Sexton, who won 118 Ireland caps as a player. "But I know Tadhg as a person, first and foremost, and I don't think that's something he would have done. "So I just have to back him in that regard, but we'll see what happens with the disciplinary hearing." Sexton added that Furlong had started the season "pretty well" for Leinster after an injury-hit last campaign. "His body's good, which is always a good thing with Tadhg. When his body's good, he tends to play really well." If similar action was taken against Furlong, he could miss Ireland's four matches in November against Argentina, Fiji, South Africa and then the finals weekend of the Nations Championship in London. He could also be banned for Leinster's Investec Champions Cup Pool match with Sale, as well as the festive inter-provincial derbies with Ulster and Munster. On Monday, after the news that Furlong had been cited, Leinster assistant coach Robin McBryde said it was "completely out of character for Tadhg". "There is a process in place and we'll allow that process to run its course," McBryde said. "I can't even remember him having a yellow card, never mind anything else, in the years I have been working with him. Hopefully that will be taken into consideration.
